name: ImageNet Library of Functions for Global Optimization
description: Knowledge of search-landscape features of BlackBox Optimization (BBO) problems offers valuable information in light of the Algorithm Selection and/or Configuration problems. Exploratory Landscape Analysis (ELA) models have gained success in identifying predefined human-derived features and in facilitating portfolio selectors to address those challenges. Unlike ELA approaches, the current study proposes to transform the identification problem into an image recognition problem, with a potential to detect conception-free, machine-driven landscape features. To this end, we introduce the notion of Landscape Images, which enables us to generate imagery instances per a benchmark function, and then target the classification challenge over a diverse generalized dataset of functions. We address it as a supervised multi-class image recognition problem and apply basic artificial neural network models to solve it. The efficacy of our approach is numerically validated on the noise free BBOB and IOHprofiler benchmarking suites. This evident successful learning is another step toward automated feature extraction and local structure deduction of BBO problems. By using this definition of landscape images, and by capitalizing on existing capabilities of image recognition algorithms, we foresee the construction of an ImageNet-like library of functions for training generalized detectors that rely on machine-driven features.
reputation: A research-oriented benchmark proposing a novel representation (landscape images) for black‑box optimization communities; limited adoption beyond ELA/BBO researchers so far.
notes: Non-LLM, synthetic / generated-image dataset derived from BBOB and IOHprofiler functions; potential for overfitting to generation artifacts, class imbalance, and limited dataset scale compared to mainstream image benchmarks.
